record.title: Caller-selected foreign staff references may disclose staff names through sales and shifts
record.description: Source review supports, but does not dynamically demonstrate, an organization A member attaching a known organization B staff UUID to an A sale or cash shift and receiving B staff.name. This changes attribution in A-owned records; it does not establish mutation of B staff, B sales, B shifts or payroll. Live-session authentication and tenant-scoped parent selectors do not validate the explicitly supplied staff reference. UUID knowledge is a prerequisite; no discovery mechanism is established. No comparable baseline was supplied and no severity is assigned.
record.claimed_root_cause: Sales and shift creation accept a UUID-shaped cashierStaffId without checking staff.organizationId, outletId, isActive or deletedAt. The explicit selector overrides the tenant-scoped authenticated/fallback staff identity. Single-column staff foreign keys enforce existence, not tenant binding. Subsequent sales lookup and shift join resolve staff names by ID alone. Tenant binding is explicitly required by PRD.md:124-125; outlet/lifecycle validation is appropriate defense but its precise business policy should be agreed before treating every inactive or historical reference as independently unauthorized.

trace.description: Authenticated outlet-context POST accepts caller JSON, parses createSaleSchema and returns createSale output; a UUID Idempotency-Key is required.
cashierStaffId is optional and checked only for UUID syntax.
The caller-selected staff UUID takes precedence over ctx.staffId in the sale insert. Warehouse, products and stock are checked separately, without a staff ownership check.
Reads staff.id and staff.name by staff ID alone; returns name and resolved staffId without organization, outlet or lifecycle predicates.
The cashier value resolved after transaction commit is included in the response returned by the HTTP route.

evidence.description: Tenant-owned queries must filter organization; line 125 makes sales and shifts outlet-scoped.
Reloads unrevoked session, enabled user and organization membership; lines 55-79 build outlet context and tenant-scoped linked staff. These checks do not bind a body-supplied cashierStaffId.
Requires a nonempty active outlet only; performs no staff-reference validation.
Replay cache lookup binds organization, user, method, path and key; this prevents unrelated cached responses but does not validate staff ownership on a fresh request.
Open shift lookup always filters organization and outlet, and may fall back to any open A shift. A foreign staff selector does not select a B shift and no open shift is required to persist a sale.
Sale list is tenant/outlet scoped; detail likewise uses both at lines 217-225. These parent predicates do not constrain getCashierDetails.
POS accepts the same optional UUID cashierStaffId; pos.service.ts:11-12 forwards input to the same createSale service.
Shift open requires authentication, an outlet and owner/admin/staff authorization, then parses openShiftSchema. Listing at lines 24-35 returns repository cashierStaffName.
Shift open accepts optional UUID cashierStaffId; staffId is not a declared HTTP schema field, so the service body.staffId alias is not needed for this trace.
An explicit cashierStaffId bypasses tenant-scoped getByUserId fallback. An existing open A outlet shift causes rejection at lines 25-31; otherwise lines 44-50 pass the selected ID to creation.

Listing filters cashShifts organization/outlet, but joins staff on ID alone and selects staff.name as cashierStaffName at line 48. Creation at lines 76-83 inserts organization/outlet from trusted context with the supplied staffId.
cashierStaffId references staff.id only; there is no composite tenant-binding constraint in this table definition.
cashShifts.staffId is a required single-ID foreign key; staff itself has organization/outlet plus isActive and deletedAt fields at lines 9-27.

Generated shift staff foreign key references public.staff(id) alone; sale staff foreign key does the same at line 933. No RLS policy or trigger enforcing staff tenant binding was found in reviewed migrations.
Existing stock test substitutes the transaction result and mocks getCashierDetails at line 199; it cannot establish actual staff isolation or database enforcement.

blockers: No target execution is authorized: combined OS-enforced scratch-only writes and aggregate process-tree CPU, memory, PID and disk limits have not been established. Consequently no isolated two-tenant HTTP/PostgreSQL integration result exists. The artifact promotion allowlist is empty with zero byte limits, so no target-generated result could be retained as evidence in this assignment.

Actual database enforcement and API behavior remain unobserved: an owner-controlled isolated fixture must establish whether any out-of-repository RLS, trigger or database role prevents the cross-tenant reference or staff-name lookup. Source does not refute the path.
A caller must already possess a valid foreign staff UUID. This is an exploit precondition rather than a demonstrated UUID-discovery vulnerability.

validation_plan.local: Only after the parent supplies the complete approved no-network sandbox and a bounded artifact-promotion allowlist, use an isolated disposable PostgreSQL fixture with dummy organizations A/B, an enabled A member/session, A outlet/warehouse, an active A finished-good product with stock >=1, and B staff with a unique non-sensitive marker name. With A authentication and A X-Outlet-Id, POST /api/v1/sales using a fresh UUID Idempotency-Key and body {orderType:dine_in,paymentMethod:cash,items:[{productId:<A product UUID>,qty:1}],cashierStaffId:<B staff UUID>}; inspect only the created A sale attribution and response data.cashier.name. Independently, with no open shift in A outlet, POST /api/v1/shifts/open {startingCashIdr:0,cashierStaffId:<B staff UUID>}, then GET /api/v1/shifts?page=1&limit=1 and inspect only the created shift staffId and data[0].cashierStaffName. Stop at the first marker disclosure per path; verify B staff is unchanged. Repeat with an A staff positive control and a nonexistent UUID negative control. If repaired, assert foreign references reject before any insert; resolve staff with organization/outlet and agreed active/deleted policy at creation and tenant-bound name lookup, with shared-service regression coverage for POS. Do not impose active-only name resolution on historical records without an explicit retention policy.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner should inspect only an isolated staging clone with dummy tenants using the application database role and deployed migrations, verifying any additional staff RLS/tenant trigger and whether it rejects the foreign reference or suppresses the marker name. Report request shape, status, dummy row ownership and marker presence only; do not probe production, enumerate real UUIDs, expose credentials or use real staff data.
